speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: asked the Prime Minister for the public sector corruption cases registered for investigation by CPIB in 2016 (a) what is the total amount of money involved; (b) what are the top three Ministries from which these cases originated; (c) out of the 92 cases brought forward from the previous years, how many are more than two years; and (d) what is the breakdown on the number of such cases alerted by internal staff and external sources respectively.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Corruption offences can occur at any level as long as there is greed and opportunity.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: CPIB takes a serious view of all complaints or information on suspected corruption.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: They will not hesitate to take action without fear or favour against any individuals or entities.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: However, I wish to highlight that not all cases that CPIB registered for investigation will result in prosecution.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In the last three years, the number of persons prosecuted in Court by the CPIB has been on a decline.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: However, not all the four individuals were charged for corruption offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The CPIB takes, on average, less than a year to complete investigations.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Nevertheless, this also depends on the complexity of the cases, many factors, such as the availability of witnesses or, if the case is transnational, also affect the duration of the investigations.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Even though the Singapore Public Service is known to be one of the cleanest in the world, the Government remains vigilant and constantly seek new ways to maintain the integrity of the Public Service.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: As with all corruption cases, they start and end with humans.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Ministries are required to put in place measures to ensure accountability and transparency.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Such measures include rotation of officers, having more effective supervision, holding surprise checks and conducting regular internal audits to ensure processes are in order.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: There is a reporting framework for officers to report wrongful practices of behaviour they have observed to their supervisors or the Permanent Secretary in their Ministry.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This includes the mismanagement or misuse of Government funds or actions that call into question an officer's integrity, such as in conflict of interest situations.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This helps the agency to be alerted to problems early and allow them to promptly take appropriate actions.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This is only possible because of strong political will and leadership over the years as well as the trusted Singapore Brand that is built upon our clean and honest system of governance in the business environment.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: In the original question, I asked what is the breakdown of the number of cases alerted by internal and external sources respectively.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: And my supplementary question is, out of the 18 cases involving public employees registered for investigations, four were prosecuted in Court.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The rest were given warning or departmental actions.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: So, what are the grounds for recommending such action in lieu of prosecution for these cases from the Public Sector?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The answer is three and one to make the four.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because when a case is being prosecuted, once it has breached our rules and our guidelines, it will be prosecuted in Court.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If let us say, there are no clear evidence for us to take the person to task, then if there are any other things that are tantamount to any wrongdoing but not enough for us to cross the threshold, then there may be other administration guidelines for us to take punishment action if someone is in the wrong.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Mr Png, please address your queries to the Chair.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: There were 18 cases registered for investigation for the Public Sector.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Four were sent to Court but then the rest, they said that they administered warning and given departmental actions.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: So, I just want to know what are the grounds for recommending such action, in lieu of prosecution, since they are already registered for investigation.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: First, let me clarify that registered for investigation does not prove that they are guilty.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It just means that there might be a case for us to follow up and pursue.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Out of the cases mentioned, four were eventually prosecuted in Court.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Where there is not sufficient evidence of severity to prosecute them in Court, we will see whether there is any ground for us to take other actions.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: There is always a range of actions required for us.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But for those cases that go to the Court, that is when there are very clear guidelines as to when you crossed the legal threshold.
